(BY SRI SHIVAKUMAR S. BADAWADAGI, ADVOCATE FOR R1;
 R2 - SERVICE OF NOTICE HELD SUFFICIENT.)

THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL IS FILED UNDER  SECTION 173(1) OF MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, 1988, PRAYING TO SET  ASIDE THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 20.11.2015, PASSED BY  THE ADDITIONAL M.A.C.T., KUMTA (ITINERARY SITTING AT  ANKOLA), IN MVC NO.64/2012, BY ALLOWING THIS APPEAL, ETC.,.
 -2-  NC: 2023:KHC-D:12486  MFA No. 100446 of 2016  THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the insurance company challenging the judgment and award dated 20.11.2015, passed by the tribunal, in MVC No.64/2012, questioning the liability fixed on the insurance company to pay compensation on the ground that the driving licence is fake one.
2. The factum of accident, the claimant sustaining injuries in the accident are not in dispute in this case.
The only disputed fact is that whether driving licence is proved to be fake licence or not as contended by the insurance company.

3. Heard the arguments and perused the material placed before the Court.
4.
The tribunal while awarding compensation has fixed liability on the appellant insurance company by NC: 2023:KHC-D:12486 holding that the driver was holding valid and effective driving licence.
It is argued by the learned counsel for appellant that the driving licence of the driver is fake one.
5. The official of the appellant company is examined as RW.1 deposing that the driving licence is fake one.

Copy of the driving licence is produced before the tribunal by the claimant (which is unmarked) and based on that the appellant has sent copy of that driving licence to the RTO,
Varanasi.

In turn the RTO, Varanasi, has furnished a letter as Ex.R.2 that since the cover page on the said driving licence is not legible, unable to furnish whether RTO, Varanasi, has issued the driving licence or not.

When the claimant has produced the driving licence to the tribunal and when it is contending by the appellant that the said driving licence is fake one, then it is burden on the insurance company to prove that the said driving licence is fake one.
But the appellant insurance company has not discharged its burden to prove that the driving licence is fake one.

sentences.text: The evidence of respondent No.1 is concerned and more particularly the cross-examination of RW.1 official of appellant insurance company, it is emerged that the appellant insurance company has not made effort to prove the driving licence is fake one except saying orally in examination-in-chief.

The appellant insurance company has office at Varanasi or around Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh and the appellant could have made more effort to get particulars from RTO, Varanasi,
proving the driving licence is fake one, but the appellant has not made such effort, even though it is very much possible for the appellant insurance company.
Therefore when the appellant has taken a contention that the driving licence is fake one, when it is burden on the insurance company to prove the same, but this burden is not discharged.
Therefore there is no merit found in the grounds urged by the appellant insurance company.

7. It is argued by the learned counsel for appellant that the appellant has taken out paper publication at NC: 2023:KHC-D:12486 Mumbai since address of the 2nd respondent owner of truck is shown at Mumbai, calling upon to produce the driving licence.
But this exercise of the appellant is a futile exercise.
Just by putting paper publication calling upon the owner of truck to produce the driving licence is not feasible and practical one.

The appellant could have put effort by summoning respondent No.2 owner but without doing that effort, publishing in newspaper calling upon to produce the driving licence is somewhat ridicule and absurd situation.
Hence the appeal is liable to be dismissed.

8. In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is dismissed.
ii) The judgment and award dated 20.11.2015, passed by the Addl. MACT, Kumta,
Itinerary sitting at Ankola, in MVC No.64/2012, stands confirmed.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:12486 iii) The amount in deposit shall be transmitted to the tribunal.
 iv) No order as to costs.

SD/-
